subject: Finova decision criteria — latency, cost & deployment follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Rogers <ethan.rogers@finova.com>, Sita Menon <sita.menon@finova.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Oct 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Finova decision criteria — latency, cost & deployment follow-up

Thanks again for the time today — great discussion. I wanted to recap the key decision criteria you called out and propose clear next steps so we can align stakeholders on the buying process. Notes from the call: 

- Primary decision criteria:
  - Latency: target p95 <= 200ms for 1–2k RPS bursts (mostly short prompts, avg tokens/request ~75)
  - Cost: goal to keep inference spend predictable; target is to be materially below current internal cost baseline (Finova asked for < 40% of current per-inference cost)
  - Deployment mode: initial preference for Dedicated capacity (for predictable throughput + data isolation), with Private (VPC) considered if procurement requires customer-managed control plane
  - SLA: production SLA required (uptime + latency SLOs) and escalation paths for incidents

- Security/procurement asks you flagged: SOC 2 report, DPA language, data residency options, and timing for vendor onboarding/procurement packet
- Stakeholders to involve next: Procurement/legal (contract + DPA), Security (SOC 2 + architecture review), and the economic buyer (VP of Product / CFO for cost approval)

Attached: decision-criteria template (please fill in the stakeholder columns), and I included the SOC2 report link in case you want to share with Security.

Proposed next steps:
1) Can you share the stakeholder names & preferred contact (security, procurement, economic buyer) by EOD Thu?
2) We will schedule a 30-minute technical deep-dive with our solutions engineer (Dev) to validate latency/cost assumptions — proposed window next week (Mon/Tue).
3) I will send a mutual action plan (MAP) template once we have the stakeholder list so procurement can track milestones.

Happy to adjust — want to make procurement as frictionless as possible.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: redwood-decision-criteria-template.xlsx

From: Ethan Rogers <ethan.rogers@finova.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sita Menon <sita.menon@finova.com>
Date: Wed, 6 Oct 2027 09:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Finova decision criteria — latency, cost & deployment follow-up

Thanks, Marissa — helpful recap. A few clarifying items from our side before we pull in procurement/security: 

- Latency: when you quote p95 <= 200ms, is that for user-facing single-turn generation on Dedicated? How do numbers change for contexts with longer histories (500–1k tokens) and for the Private/VPC option?
- Cost: can you map the expected unit economics to our workload? For reference, our baseline is ~2.2M inference requests/mo with average 75 tokens out and 40 tokens in per request; we want a model that keeps incremental spend predictable (finance will ask for a 6–12 month forecast).
- Deployment lead time: procurement asked whether Dedicated or Private will add multi-week setup time and whether we need an on-prem appliance for any of the compliance asks. 

We’ll start compiling names for Security and Procurement — I should have the stakeholder list and initial questions by Friday. Also, can you share a short doc for what your SLA covers exactly (latency SLO, uptime, credits)?

Thanks,
Ethan
VP, Engineering | Finova
ethan.rogers@finova.com

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Rogers <ethan.rogers@finova.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 8 Oct 2027 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Finova decision criteria — latency, cost & deployment follow-up

Looping in Dev (solutions engineering) to answer the perf/deployment specifics — quick replies below: 

- p95 <= 200ms: achievable on Dedicated for short contexts (<= 200 tokens total) for single-turn requests with optimized batching and KV caching. For longer histories (500–1k tokens) p95 will increase — expect a ~1.5–2x latency delta depending on model family and sequence processing. We can run a focused perf test using a representative trace to validate real numbers.
- Private/VPC: performance is comparable to Dedicated if we provision equivalent GPU types; however, onboarding time is longer (typically 2–6 weeks depending on network provisioning and customer firewall rules).
- Cost mapping: we can produce a simple TCO model tied to your monthly RPS and token distribution. For initial planning we’ll prepare a 6–month spend forecast and an expected cost-per-1M-tokens baseline aligned to the model families we recommend.
- SLA: Redwood’s standard Dedicated SLA includes availability commitments (SLA crediting on monthly uptime < 99.9%) and latency SLOs for pinned model routes. We’ll surface exact SLO numbers in the MAP and the contract.

Next steps from my side:
- Can Finova share a small sample trace (anonymized) so we can run a targeted perf run?
- I’ll attach our perf runbook and a short tech note on deployment timelines.

Regards,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.com

Attachments: perf-runbook.pdf
